If the characteristic equation of the differential equation

The characteristic equation is given as
\[\begin{aligned} \left(m^{2}+2(x)+1\right) &=0 \\ m_{1}, m_{2} &=\frac{-2 x_{1} \pm \sqrt{4 x^{2}-4}}{2} \end{aligned}\\ \text{since both roots are equal i.e.} \\ \begin{aligned} m_{1}=& m_{2} \\ \frac{-2 \alpha+\sqrt{4 \alpha^{2}-4}}{2} &=\frac{-2\alpha \cdot-\sqrt{4 a^{2}-4}}{2} \\ \sqrt{4\left(1^{2}-4\right.} &=-\sqrt{4 c^{2}-4} \\ 2 \sqrt{4 c^{2}-4} &=0 \\ 4 \alpha^{2}-4 &=0 \\ \alpha^{2} &=1 \\ \alpha &=\pm 1 \end{aligned}\]

questions.question:
An FIR system is described by the system function
\(H(z)=1+\frac{7}{2}z^{-1}+\frac{3}{2}z^{-2}\)
The system is
questions.explanation:
Minimum phase \(\Rightarrow\) all zeroes are inside the unit circle.
For maximum phase, all the zeroes are outside the unit circle.
\(H(z)=1+\frac{7}{2} z^{-1}+\frac{3}{2} z^{-2}=0\)
\(2 z^{2}+6 z+z+3=0\)
\((2 z+1)(z+3)=0\)
\(z_{1}=-\frac{1}{2}\) (inside the unit circle)
\(z_{2}=-3\) (outside the unit circle)
\(\therefore\) Mixed phase.

questions.subject: signals-and-systems
questions.question:
Consider the periodic square wave in the figure shown.

The ratio of the power in the \(7^{th}\) harmonic to the power in the \(5^{th}\) harmonic for this waveform is closest in value to ______.
questions.explanation:
\[\begin{aligned} X(\omega) &=\sum_{K=-\infty}^{\infty} 2 \pi a_{k} \delta\left(0-K \omega\right) \\ a_{K} &=\frac{1}{2 \pi} \int_{0}^{2} x(t) e^{-j K \omega_{0} t} d t \end{aligned}\]
\[\begin{aligned} &=\frac{1}{2 \pi}\left\{\int_{0}^{1} 1 \cdot e^{-j K \omega_{o} t} d \omega-\int_{1}^{2} 1 \cdot e^{-j K \omega_{o} t} d \omega\right\}\\ &=\frac{1}{2\pi}\left[\frac{1}{-j K \omega_{o}}[e^{-j K \omega_{o}}-1]-\frac{1}{-j K \omega_{o}}[e^{(-j 2K \omega_{o})}-e^{(-j 2K \omega_{o})}] \right ]\\ &=\frac{1}{2\pi}\left[\frac{e^{-j K \omega_{o}l2}}{j K \omega_{o}}.2j\sin\frac{K\omega_{o}}{2}-\frac{1}{j K \omega_{o}}e^{-\frac{j K \omega_{o}3}{2}}\left(2j\sin\frac{K\omega_{0}}{2} \right ) \right ]\\ &=\frac{1}{\pi}\left[\frac{\sin \frac{K \omega_{o}}{2}}{K \omega_{o}}\left(e^{-j K \omega_{0}}\right)\left(e^{\frac{j K \omega_{0}}{2}}-e^{-\frac{K_{m_{2}}}{2}}\right)\right] \\ &=\frac{1}{\pi}\left(\frac{\sin K \omega_{0} / 2}{K \omega_{o}}\right) e^{-j K \omega_{0}} \times 2 j \sin \left(\frac{\left.K_{\left(0_{0}\right.}\right)}{2}\right) \\ &=\frac{1}{\pi^{2}} \frac{\left(\sin K \frac{\pi}{2}\right)^{2}}{K} 2 j \times \cos K \pi \end{aligned}\\\]
\(7^{\text {th }}\) harmonic power \(=\left(2 \pi a_{7}\right)^{2}\)
\(5^{\text {th }}\) harmonic power \(=\left(2 \pi a_{5}\right)^{2}\)
\(Ratio =\left(\frac{a_{7}}{a_{5}}\right)^{2}=\left(\frac{5}{7}\right)^{2}=\frac{25}{49}=0.51\)

questions.subject: communication-systems
questions.question:
The capacity of a band-limited additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel is given by \(C=Wlog_{2}(1+\frac{P}{\sigma ^{2}W})\) bits per second (bps), where W is the channel bandwidth, P is the average power received and \({\sigma^{2}}\) is the one sided power spectral density of the AWGN.
For a fixed \(\frac{P}{\sigma ^{2}}=1000\), the channel capacity (in kbps) with infinite bandwidth \((W\rightarrow \infty )\) is approximately.
questions.explanation: \[\begin{aligned} C&=W \log _{2}\left(1+\frac{P}{\sigma^{2} W}\right) \\ C&=\frac{P}{\sigma^{2}} \times \frac{\sigma^{2}}{P} W \log _{2}\left(1+\frac{P}{\sigma^{2} W}\right)\\ \text{when }\quad W &\rightarrow \infty \\ C_{\infty}&=\frac{P}{\sigma^{2}} \lim _{w \rightarrow \infty} \frac{\sigma^{2} W}{P} \log _{2}\left(1+\frac{P}{\sigma^{2} W}\right)\\ \text{as }\quad W &\rightarrow \infty, \frac{\sigma^{2} W}{P}\text{ also }\rightarrow \infty \\ \therefore C_{\infty}&=\frac{P}{\sigma^{2}} \frac{\lim _{\alpha} \frac{\sigma^{2} W}{P} \log _{2}\left(1+\frac{1}{\frac{\sigma^{2} W}{P}}\right)}{P} \\ &\quad \left[\because \lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} x \log _{2}\left(1+\frac{1}{x}\right)=\log\right]\\ C_{\infty} &=\frac{P}{\sigma^{2}} \log _{2} e\\ C_{\infty} &=1.44\frac{P}{\sigma^{2}} \end{aligned}\]

questions.question: If \(\vec{r}=x\hat{a}_{x}+y\hat{a}_{y}+z\hat{a}_{z}\) and \(|\vec{r}|=r,\) then \(div(r^{2}\bigtriangledown (ln \; r))=\)____.

\[\begin{aligned} &\text{div}\left(r^{2} \nabla(l \cap)\right) \\ &=\text{div}\left(r^{2} \cdot \frac{1}{r}\left(\frac{\partial r}{\partial} \hat{a}_{x}+\frac{\partial r}{\partial y} \hat{a}_{y}+\frac{\partial r}{\partial z} \hat{a}_{z}\right)\right) \\ &=\text{div}\left(r \frac{\partial r}{\partial x} \hat{a}_{x}+\partial \frac{\partial r}{\partial y} \hat{a}_{y}+r \frac{\partial r}{\partial z} \hat{a}_{z}\right) &\ldots(i) \end{aligned}\]

questions.subject: network-theory
questions.question: In the h-parameter model of the 2-port network given in the figure shown, the value of \(h_{22}\) (in S ) in _____.
questions.explanation:
When two, two port networks are connected in parallel then individual Y-parameters are added. Therefore from the given network,


For network ( 1) Y-parameter is,
\[Y_{1}=\left[\begin{array}{cc} \frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} \\ -\frac{1}{3} & \frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{3} \end{array}\right]\]
Similarly for network (2).
\[\begin{aligned} Y_{2}=&\left[\begin{array}{rr} 1 & -\frac{1}{2} \\ -\frac{1}{2} & 1 \end{array}\right] \\ \text { Thus, } \quad Y=Y_{1}+Y_{2}=&\left[\begin{array}{cc} \frac{5}{3} & -\frac{5}{6} \\ -\frac{5}{6} & \frac{5}{3} \end{array}\right] \\ \therefore \quad I_{1}=& Y_{11} V_{1}+Y_{12} V_{2} \end{aligned}\]
\[\begin{aligned} &=\frac{5}{3} Y_{1}-\frac{5}{6} V_{2} &\ldots(i)\\ I_{2} &=Y_{21} V_{1}+Y_{22} V_{2} \\ &=-\frac{5}{6} V_{1}+\frac{5}{3} V_{2} &\ldots(ii)\\ \text { Also } \quad h_{22} &=\left.\frac{I_{2}}{V_{2}}\right|_{I_{1}=0} \end{aligned}\]
\(\therefore\) From equation (i), we get,
\(V_{1}=\frac{1}{2} V_{2} \qquad \ldots(iii)\)
and from equation (ii) and (iii), we get,
\(h_{22}=\frac{I_{2}}{V_{2}}=\frac{15}{12}=1.25\)

questions.subject: network-theory
questions.question: In the figure shown, the capacitor is initially uncharged. Which one of the following expressions describes the current I(t) (in mA) for t > 0 ?
questions.explanation:
Converting the given circuit into frequency domain and applying KCL at V(s)


We get,
\[\begin{array}{l} \frac{V(s)-\frac{5}{s}}{R_{1}}+\frac{V(s)}{R_{2}}+\frac{V(s)}{\frac{1}{C s}}=0 \quad\ldots(i)\\ \because \quad R_{1}=1 \mathrm{k} \Omega, R_{2}=2 \mathrm{k} \Omega \text { and } C=1 \mu \mathrm{F} \end{array}\]
Using the components value we get,
\(V(s)\left[\frac{1}{1}+\frac{1}{2}+s\right]=\frac{5}{s}\)

questions.question: Assume electronic charge \(q=1.6 \times 10^{-19}C\), kT/q=25mV and electron mobility \(\mu _{n}=1000cm^{2} /V-s\) . If the concentration gradient of electrons injected into a P-type silicon sample is \(1 \times 10^{21}/cm^{4}\), the magnitude of electron diffusion current density (in \(A/cm^{2}\)) is _____.

questions.question: Consider an abrupt PN junction (at T = 300 K) shown in the figure. questions.explanation:
For abrupt \(P^{+}\) N junction
\(E_{\max }\) is given:
\[\begin{aligned} E_{\max } &=\frac{-q N_{0} x_{n}}{\epsilon_{s}}\qquad\left[\begin{array}{c} \because N_{A}>>N_{D} \\ W \simeq x_{n} \end{array}\right] \\ \Rightarrow E_{\max }&=\frac{-1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 10^{16} \times 0.2 \times 10^{-4}}{1.044 \times 10^{-12}} \\ E_{\max } &=-30.65 \times 10^{3} \mathrm{V} / \mathrm{cm} \\ E_{\max } &=-30.65 \mathrm{kV} / \mathrm{cm} \end{aligned}\]

questions.subject: electronic-devices
questions.question:
When a silicon diode having a doping concentration of \(N_{A}=9\times10^{16}cm^{-3}\) on p
-side and \(N_{D}=1\times10^{16}cm^{-3}\) on n-side is reverse biased, the total depletion width is found to be 3 \(\mu\) m. Given that the permittivity of silicon is \(1.04\times10^{-12}\) F/cm, the depletion width on the p-side and the maximum electric field in the depletion region, respectively, are
questions.explanation:
We know that
\[\begin{aligned} \frac{N_{A}}{N_{D}}&=\frac{x_{n}}{x_{p}}\\ So, \frac{N_{A}}{N_{D}}+1&=\frac{x_{n}}{x_{p}}+1 \\ \frac{N_{A}+N_{D}}{N_{D}}&=\frac{x_{n}+x_{p}}{x_{p}}\\ \frac{10^{17}}{10^{16}} &=\frac{3 \mu m}{x_{p}} \\ \therefore \quad x_{p} &=0.3 \mu \mathrm{m}\\ \text{and}\\ E_{\max }&=\frac{q N_{A} x_{p}}{\epsilon_{s}}=\frac{q N_{D} x_{n}}{\epsilon_{s}} \\ \therefore E_{\max } &=\frac{1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 9 \times 10^{16} \times 0.3 \times 10^{-4}}{1.04 \times 10^{-12}} \\ E_{\max } &=4.15 \times 10^{5} \mathrm{V} / \mathrm{cm} \end{aligned}\]

Consider a discrete-time signal
\[x[n]=\left\{\begin{matrix} n & for \; 0\leq n\leq 10\\ 0&otherwise \end{matrix}\right.\]
If y[n] is the convolution of x[n] with itself, the value of y[4] is _____.
questions.explanation: \[\begin{array}{l} x[n]=\left\{\begin{array}{ll} n & \text { for } 0 \leq n \leq 10 \\ 0 & \text { otherwise } \end{array}\right. \\ y[n]=\sum_{K=\infty}^{\infty} x(k) x(n-k) \\ y[4]=\sum_{k=0}^{10} x(k) x(4-k) \\ =x(0) x(4)+x(1) x(3)+x(2) x(2)+x(3) x(1)+0 \\ =0+(1 \times 3)+(2 \times 2)+(3 \times 1) \\ =10 \end{array}\]

questions.question:
The input-output relationship of a causal stable LTI system is given as
\(y[n] = \alpha\) y[n -1]+ \(\beta x[n]\)
If the impulse response h[n] of this system satisfies the condition \(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty }h[n]=2\), the relationship between \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) is
questions.explanation:
Input-output relation is given as
\[\begin{aligned} y[n]&=\alpha_{\mathcal{Y}}(n-1)+\beta x[n] \\ \text{Taking Z-transform, }\\ r(z)&=\alpha z^{-1} \quad Y (z)+\beta X(z) \\ Y(z)&\left[1-\alpha z^{-1}\right]=\beta X(z) \\ \frac{\gamma(z)}{X(z)}&=H(z)=\frac{\beta}{1-\alpha z^{-1}} \\ h[n]&=\beta \cdot \alpha^{n} u[n] \\ \text{Also }&\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} h[n]=2 \Rightarrow \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \beta \cdot \alpha^{n} u[n]=2 \\ \frac{\beta}{1-\alpha}&=2 \Rightarrow \beta=2-2 \alpha \\ \Rightarrow 2 a &=2-\beta \\ \alpha &=1-\frac{\beta}{2} \end{aligned}\]

questions.question:
An unforced linear time invariant (LTI) system is represented by
\[\begin{vmatrix} \dot{x}_{1}\\ \dot{x}_{2} \end{vmatrix}=\begin{vmatrix} -1 & 0\\ 0&-2 \end{vmatrix}\begin{vmatrix} x_{1}\\ x_{2} \end{vmatrix}\]
If the initial conditions are \(x_{1}(0)=1 \; and \; x_{2}(0)=-1\), the solution of the state equation is
questions.explanation:
\[\begin{aligned}\left[\begin{array}{l}\dot{x}_{1} \\ \dot{x}_{2}\end{array}\right] &=\left[\begin{array}{cc}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l}x_{1} \\ x_{2}\end{array}\right] \\ \dot{x}_{1} &=-x_{1}+0 x_{2} \\ \dot{x}_{2} &=0 x_{1}-2 x_{2} \end{aligned}\]
Applying Laplace transform on both equations
\[\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow s X_{1}(s)-x_{1}(0)&=-X_{1}(s) \\ X_{1}(s)[s+1]&=X_{1}(0) \quad &\text{given }x_{1}(0)=1 \\ X_{1}(s)&=\frac{1}{s+1} \\ \Rightarrow \quad e^{-t}&=x_{1}(t)\\ \Rightarrow \quad s X_{2}(s)-X_{2}(0)&=-2 X_{2}(s) \\ (s+2) X_{2}(s)&=X_{2}(0) &X_{2}(0)=-1 \\ X_{2}(s)&=-\frac{1}{s+2} \\ x_{2}(t)&=-e^{-2 t} \end{aligned}\]

Assume quantization voltage is \(V_{T h}\)
For outputs of quantizer to have equal probability
\[\begin{aligned} \rightarrow P\left(X S V_{T h}\right)=& P\left(X \geq V_{T h}\right) \\ \int_{0}^{v_{T}} f_{X}(x) d x &=\int_{V_{m}} f_{X}(x) d x \\ \int_{0}^{V} 2 e^{-2 x} d x &=\int_{V_{T h}}^{\infty} 2 e^{-2 x} d x \\ e^{-2 x V_{i h}} &=\frac{1}{2} \\ V_{T h} &=0.346 \end{aligned}\]

questions.subject: electromagnetics
questions.question:
For a rectangular waveguide of internal dimensions \(a \times b(a \gt b)\), the cur-off
frequency for the \(TE_{11}\) mode is the arithmetic mean of the cut-off frequencies for \(TE_{10}\) mode and \(TE_{20}\) mode. If a = \(\sqrt{5}\) cm, the value of b (in cm) is______.
questions.explanation:
Cut-off frequency of a rectangular waveguide is
\[\begin{aligned} f_{c}&=\frac{c}{2 \pi} \sqrt{\left(\frac{m \pi}{a}\right)^{2}+\left(\frac{n\pi}{b}\right)^{2}} \\ f_{c} \text{ for }\quad T E_{10}&=\frac{c}{2 \pi} \sqrt{\left(\frac{1 \pi}{a}\right)^{2}}=\frac{c}{2 a} \\ f_{c} \text{ for }\quad T E_{20}&=\frac{c}{2 \pi} \sqrt{\left(\frac{2 \pi}{a}\right)^{2}}=\frac{c}{2 a} \\ f_{c} \text { for } \quad T E_{11} &=\frac{c}{2 \pi} \sqrt{\left(\frac{\pi}{a}\right)^{2}}+\left(\frac{\pi}{b}\right)^{2} \\ &=\frac{c}{2} \sqrt{\left(\frac{1}{a}\right)^{2}+\left(\frac{1}{b}\right)^{2}} \\ \text { Given, } f_{C T_{11}} &=\frac{f_{C_{I E 10}}+f_{C I E_{20}}}{2} \end{aligned}\]
\[\begin{aligned} \frac{c}{2} \sqrt{\left(\frac{1}{a}\right)^{2}+\left(\frac{1}{b}\right)^{2}}&=\frac{\frac{c}{2 a}+\frac{c}{a}}{2} \\ \sqrt{\left(\frac{1}{a}\right)^{2}+\left(\frac{1}{b}\right)^{2}}&=\frac{1}{2 a}+\frac{1}{a}=\frac{3}{2 a} \\ \left(\frac{1}{a}\right)^{2}+\left(\frac{1}{b}\right)^{2}&=\frac{9}{4 a^{2}} \\ \Rightarrow \quad\left(\frac{1}{b}\right)^{2} &=\frac{5}{4 a^{2}} \\ b &=\frac{2 a}{\sqrt{5}}=\frac{2 \times \sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{5}} \\ &=2 \mathrm{cm} \end{aligned}\]
